text: Scaling up or deleting the overloaded pods wouldn't fix this — with no spread rule, the scheduler could just as easily rebuild the exact same imbalance a few minutes later.
Theo adds a real topologySpreadConstraints block to checkout-api's Deployment: maxSkew 1, spread by availability zone, DoNotSchedule if it can't be satisfied, scoped to checkout-api's own pods.

Applying it live is safe because kubectl apply triggers a rolling update, not an in-place restart — governed by the Deployment's rollout strategy and the PodDisruptionBudget set back in Lesson 8, which guarantees a minimum number of pods stay available the whole time.

With the constraint in place and twelve replicas across three zones, the scheduler now has to land close to four pods per zone. Next lesson: confirming it actually worked, under the sale's continuing real load.
